annotations.title: Kundli milan: how well two people match for marriage (36 gunas)

description: Checks how well two people match for marriage in the Indian (Vedic) tradition, from both people's birth details: a score out of 36 with what each of its eight parts means, and whether either person has the Mars placement (Manglik) that families often ask about. Useful when the user is thinking about marriage or a relationship, weighing a proposal or a rishta, or their family has asked for a kundli match: "match my kundli with hers", "kundli milan", "guna milan", "how many gunas match", "kundli milao", "kitne gun milte hain", "rishta aaya hai, kundli match karo", Manglik, Nadi or Bhakoot dosha. Computed by AstroCalc's engine. Returns the Ashtakoota total and band, all 8 kootas (Varna, Vashya, Tara, Yoni, Graha Maitri, Gana, Bhakoot, Nadi) with points and a plain-language meaning, which doshas are cancelled by classical exceptions, each person's Manglik status and the pair verdict, a caveat, and a link to the full free report. Each person needs a birth date and place; time is optional. Details are used in memory only and not stored. The score is one traditional input, not a decision about a relationship.

lang.description: Language of the text fields: 'en' (English, default) or 'hi' (Hindi).

person_a.description: Birth details of the first person.

gender.description: Optional. Classical milan reads the boy's chart against the girl's; with a male/female pair the order is set by gender, otherwise person_a is read as the boy.

lat.description: Birth latitude in decimal degrees (north positive). Give together with lon.

lon.description: Birth longitude in decimal degrees (east positive). Give together with lat.

place.description: Birth city or town, e.g. 'Lucknow' or 'Pune, Maharashtra, India'. The best match is used (Indian cities preferred); call search_place first if unsure. Not needed when lat and lon are given.

time.description: Local clock time of birth, 24-hour HH:MM (e.g. '06:45', '21:10'); '6:45 am' / '9:10 PM' also work. Use 'unknown' (or omit) if not known: noon is used, the Moon sign stays reliable but the Lagna is approximate.

person_b.description: Birth details of the second person.
